walkthroughs.name: Why this change
walkthroughs.summary: Six beats, for somebody deciding whether to pay for it

beats.heading: Agents author the drawing
beats.body: Placement, sizing, routes and labels are persisted geometry. People repair the picture so that it explains the architecture, and the repair is the work.

beats.heading: The board commits before anything is announced
beats.body: Claims and versions protect the authoritative file; panes and agents hear about a change only after the bytes have landed. That part is not changing.

beats.heading: Meaning becomes canonical
beats.body: An agent states responsibilities, containment and relationships. Nothing states a coordinate, because there is nowhere to put one, and the renderer supplies hierarchy consistently.

beats.heading: One edit updates the whole family
beats.body: A change to the state a proposal came from reaches every draft under it in the same write. Safe changes arrive; real disagreements stay visible, with the draft's own content still coherent.

beats.heading: One architecture, two explanations
beats.body: The parts and the order they act in are the same identities read two ways, and a walkthrough moves attention through the story.

beats.heading: Adoption moves current and keeps history
beats.body: A competing proposal can become the architecture of record. What it replaced freezes under its own name, and ancestry is untouched: adoption is a designation, not a lineage.
